items.content:
You can now watch a graph engineering run from Hermes Desktop.

A big Hermes task used to mean scrolling back through the chat to find out which part was still running. Now you start it in Desktop and watch it instead. Desktop keeps the plan above the composer, and the Oh My Hermes pane on the right follows the run: each lane and the model it runs on, what's running, what failed and got repaired, and the verify step that has to pass before anything is called done. The status bar shows the same count, so a glance is enough when the pane is closed.

Oh My Hermes (OMH) is an open-source operating layer for Hermes Agent. You keep talking to Hermes the way you already do. Its graph engineering workflow turns your goal into a graph of small tasks, picks a skill and a model for each one, runs the independent ones in parallel, and checks the result before it reports back. It ships 100+ specialist skills (frontend, backend, Rust, security review, verification gates), and the router loads the ones a task needs, so you never call them by name.

It doesn't patch or replace Hermes. The Desktop pane is a plugin that comes with OMH: install, then turn it on under Capabilities → Plugins in Desktop.

The clip is the real Desktop app; the run in it is illustrative.

Github: https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E
